limits: The statutory exception does not establish the date or nature of landlord knowledge.
Initial absence of consent is distinct from later alleged acquiescence.
The Court did not decide whether acquiescence, if actually proved, would legally defeat the statutory ground.
The available statutory ground must be distinguished from the final possession decree.
conditional_rules.stage: substantive entitlement under section 13(1), proviso (c)(i), Delhi and Ajmer Rent Control Act, 1952

limits: OPEN_TEXT preserves the court's fact-sensitive inferential evaluation rather than inventing an exhaustive evidentiary test.
The cited Lala Beni Ram precedent was referred to for acquiescence as legal inference, not as proof of events in this dispute.
Failure to prove knowledge of subtenancy is not affirmative proof of ignorance.
Failure to establish acquiescence does not decide its hypothetical legal effect if it were proved.
conditional_rules.stage: evidentiary assessment and legal inference on acquiescence, accepted by the Supreme Court majority

limits: A revision cannot ordinarily be used simply to reassess evidence supporting a factual finding.
Hari Shankar v. Rao Girdhari Lal Choudhury is reported as distinguishing impermissible reassessment of supported facts.
Pooran Chand v. Motilal is cited for the significance of a finding lacking evidence.
The precedents do not prove that evidence was absent in this target dispute; the target-case evidence evaluation does that.
The revisional power establishes procedural competence, not independent substantive entitlement to possession.
conditional_rules.stage: High Court revision under section 35 of the Delhi and Ajmer Rent Control Act, 1952

limits: An independent right to appeal is procedural and does not itself create permanent tenancy or immunity from ejectment.
The court did not accept the landlord's proposed automatic consequence of the Association's nonappeal.
Available appellate relief remains dependent on the merits.
conditional_rules.stage: first appeal from joint ejectment decree

limits: OPEN_TEXT is used because harmonious construction and classification of modifications versus new rights require legal evaluation.
The majority did not adopt a wholly discretionary application of the new statute.
The majority expressly declined to base its reasoning on the earlier Punjab High Court view that the proviso was merely directory.
The majority treated a wholesale substitution of the 1958 rights as improperly retrospective.
The majority did not separately decide the scope of suits and proceedings as applied to revisions.
The result is specific to the statutory saving and the substantive difference under examination.
conditional_rules.stage: Supreme Court majority interpretation of transition from the 1952 Act to the 1958 Act
